q: A learner's licence is valid for …
exp: A learner's licence is valid for 24 months from the date the test was passed.

q: Which learner's licence code do you need to learn to drive a light motor vehicle (car)?
exp: Code 1 = motorcycles, Code 2 = light motor vehicles (tare/GVM/GCM not over 3 500 kg), Code 3 = light and heavy motor vehicles.

q: What is the minimum age to obtain a Code 2 (light motor vehicle) learner's licence?
exp: Code 1: 16 years. Code 2: 17 years. Code 3: 18 years.

q: What is the minimum age to obtain a Code 1 (motorcycle) learner's licence?
exp: Code 1 (motorcycle): 16 years. Under 18 you may only ride a motorcycle of not more than 125 cm³.

q: What is the minimum age to obtain a Code 3 learner's licence?
exp: Code 3 (light and heavy motor vehicles): 18 years.

q: A Code 2 learner's licence authorises you to drive vehicles of which the tare, GVM or GCM does not exceed …
exp: A Code 2 learner may drive any motor vehicle or combination (other than a motorcycle or motor tricycle) where neither the tare, GVM nor GCM exceeds 3 500 kg.

opts.t: under the direct supervision of a person who holds a driving licence for that class of vehicle

q: When you drive with a Code 2 learner's licence, you must be …
exp: A Code 2 learner may only drive under the direct supervision of a person holding a driving licence for the applicable class of vehicle.

opts.t: carry one passenger if the passenger wears a helmet
carry a passenger only in a side-car

q: A motorcycle learner (Code 1) may …
exp: A Code 1 learner's licence does not authorise the carrying of passengers.

q: If you are under 18 and hold a Code 1 learner's licence, the motorcycle you ride may not have an engine bigger than …
exp: Under the age of 18 you may only ride a motorcycle with a cylinder capacity not exceeding 125 cm³.

q: On which form do you apply for a learner's licence?
exp: Application for a learner's licence is made at a driving licence testing centre (DLTC) on form LL1.

opts.t: A letter from your driving school
Two identical photographs, acceptable identification (and a copy) and the fee

q: Which of the following must accompany your learner's licence application?
exp: The LL1 application must be accompanied by two identical photographs, acceptable identification and a copy, the fee, and (if you are 65 or older) a medical certificate.

q: An applicant for a learner's licence must submit a medical certificate (form MC) if they are …
exp: Applicants aged 65 or older must submit a medical certificate on form MC.

opts.t: rules of the road, road traffic signs/signals/markings and the use of vehicle controls
only vehicle controls and first aid

q: The learner's licence test covers …
exp: The test covers (a) rules of the road and other legislative matters, (b) road traffic signs, signals and road markings, and (c) the use of the controls of a vehicle.

q: Which of the following would NOT on its own disqualify a person from obtaining a licence?
exp: The listed disqualifying conditions include uncontrolled epilepsy, sudden attacks of disabling giddiness or fainting, uncontrolled diabetes and defective vision. Deafness of itself is not deemed to be such a defect.

opts.t: you have changed your address in the last year
your licence has been suspended by a court and the suspension is still in force

q: You are disqualified from obtaining a learner's or driving licence if …
exp: A person is disqualified while a suspension or disqualification ordered by a competent court or authority remains in force, or if addicted to drugs or the excessive use of alcohol, among others.

q: When you permanently change your place of residence, you must notify the registering authority within …
exp: The holder of a licence must notify the registering authority of the new residential and postal address within 14 days.

opts.t: have your licence with you in the vehicle
leave your licence at home to prevent theft
only produce your licence within 7 days if asked

q: When you drive a motor vehicle on a public road you must …
exp: No person may drive on a public road unless they keep their licence (or learner's licence) with them in the vehicle.

opts.t: only if that person is licensed to drive that vehicle
if that person has a learner's licence and drives alone

q: The owner of a vehicle may allow another person to drive it on a public road …
exp: No owner or person in charge of a vehicle may permit someone to drive it unless that person is licensed to drive that vehicle.

q: Who is responsible for offences committed with a vehicle when the owner permitted someone else to use it?
exp: The owner of a vehicle is also responsible for offences committed with the vehicle if they permitted its use.

q: A motor vehicle licence and licence disc is valid for …
exp: The vehicle licence and disc are valid for 12 months from the first day of the month in which they were issued.

q: After your vehicle licence disc expires, there is a period of grace during which you may still drive the vehicle. How long is it?
exp: A vehicle may be operated for 21 days after the expiry date while the expired licence disc is displayed.

opts.t: On the lower left-hand corner of the inside of the windscreen
On the lower right-hand corner of the outside of the windscreen

q: Where must a vehicle licence disc be displayed?
exp: The disc is affixed to the lower left-hand corner on the inside of the windscreen (or in a disc holder).
src: Rules of the Road – definitions (licence disc)

opts.t: the learner drives only at night
the learner is accompanied by a person registered as a professional driver for that class of vehicle

q: A professional driving permit (PDP) is NOT needed by a learner driving a vehicle of a prescribed class if …
exp: A learner who drives such a vehicle while accompanied by a registered professional driver for that class does not need their own PDP.

opts.t: not more than 9 persons including the driver
more than 9 but not more than 16 persons including the driver
more than 16 persons including the driver

q: A "minibus" is a motor vehicle designed to carry …
exp: Motor car: not more than 9 persons. Minibus: more than 9 but not more than 16. Bus: more than 16 (all including the driver).

q: A "bus" is a motor vehicle designed or adapted to carry more than … persons (including the driver).
exp: A bus carries more than 16 persons including the driver. A midibus is a bus for more than 16 and not more than 35 persons.

q: A "motor car" is designed to carry not more than … persons, including the driver.
exp: A motor car carries not more than nine persons including the driver.

opts.t: They mean exactly the same thing
A junction is the part of the intersection on the roadway; an intersection also includes sidewalks, verges, etc.
An intersection is only where four roads meet; a junction is where three roads meet

q: What is the difference between a "junction" and an "intersection"?
exp: A junction is the area within the intersection on the improved part of the road (roadway). An intersection includes all parts of the roads, including sidewalks and verges.

opts.t: for any period, even to load passengers
for longer than reasonably necessary to load or unload persons or goods
only when the engine is switched off

q: To "park" a vehicle means to keep it stationary …
exp: "Park" means keeping a vehicle stationary for longer than is reasonably necessary to load or off-load persons or goods (not counting causes beyond the driver's control).

opts.t: between the edge of the roadway and the kerb line
between the kerb line and the property boundary
in the middle of a dual carriageway

q: The "shoulder" of the road is the part …
exp: The shoulder is the portion of the road between the edge of the roadway and the kerb line.

opts.t: the paved part of the road for vehicles
the part of the road, including the sidewalk, that is not the roadway or the shoulder
the painted island in the middle of the road

q: The "verge" is …
exp: The verge is that portion of the road, including the sidewalk, which is not the roadway or the shoulder.

opts.t: only tarred roads maintained by the government
any road or place commonly used by the public, including its verge and any bridge, ferry or drift on it

q: A "public road" includes …
exp: A public road is any road, street or place commonly used by the public or to which the public has a right of access, including the verge and any bridge, ferry or drift traversed by it.

opts.t: Any vehicle with fewer than four wheels
A motor vehicle of which the tare/GVM is not more than 3 500 kg
A vehicle that can carry up to 16 persons

q: What is a "light motor vehicle" (LMV)?
exp: An LMV is a motor vehicle with a tare/gross vehicle mass of not more than 3 500 kg.

opts.t: the mass of the vehicle without fuel
the maximum mass of the vehicle and its load as specified by the manufacturer
the mass of the load only

q: The "gross vehicle mass" (GVM) of a vehicle is …
exp: GVM is the maximum mass of the vehicle and its load as specified by the manufacturer (or the registering authority).

opts.t: ready to travel, including the spare wheel and standard equipment, but excluding fuel

q: "Tare" means the mass of a vehicle …
exp: Tare is the mass of the vehicle ready to travel, including spare wheel and standard accessories, but not including fuel.

opts.t: any part of the road used by pedestrians
a longitudinal division of a road wide enough for a single line of vehicles
the area between two stop lines

q: A "traffic lane" is …
exp: A traffic lane is a longitudinal division of a public road of sufficient width for a single line of vehicles.

opts.t: Nowhere – pedestrians may only cross at marked crossings
The part of the road at an intersection within the prolongation of the kerb line and the boundary line of the road
Any part of a road within 100 m of a school

q: Where no pedestrian crossing has been marked by a sign, which part of the road is still regarded as a pedestrian crossing?
exp: At an intersection, the portion of the road within the prolongation or connection of the kerb line and adjacent boundary line is a pedestrian crossing even when not marked.
src: Rules of the Road – definitions (pedestrian crossing)

opts.t: The vehicle has a valid licence disc
The vehicle complies with the Act and is otherwise in a fit condition to be operated on a public road
The vehicle is less than 10 years old

q: What does "roadworthy" mean?
exp: A roadworthy vehicle complies with the relevant provisions of the Act and is otherwise in a fit condition to be operated on a public road.

q: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a public road in an urban area?
exp: The general speed limits are 60 km/h in urban areas, 100 km/h outside urban areas (not freeways), and 120 km/h on freeways.

q: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a public road outside an urban area that is not a freeway?
exp: 100 km/h applies to public roads outside urban areas other than freeways.

q: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a freeway?
exp: 120 km/h applies on every freeway unless a road traffic sign indicates otherwise.

opts.t: Yes, otherwise there is no speed limit
No, it applies on all roads even if no sign is displayed

q: Must the general speed limit be shown by a road traffic sign?
exp: A general speed limit applies on all roads and does not have to be displayed by a road traffic sign.

q: What is the maximum speed for a minibus or bus conveying persons for reward?
exp: A speed limit of 100 km/h applies to buses and minibuses (conveying persons for reward).

q: What is the maximum speed for a goods vehicle with a GVM of more than 9 000 kg?
exp: 80 km/h applies to goods vehicles with GVM over 9 000 kg (and certain combinations), and to a breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle.

q: What is the maximum speed of a breakdown vehicle that is towing another vehicle?
exp: Any breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle is limited to 80 km/h.

opts.t: You may exceed the speed limit by 10%
You may exceed the speed limit for less than 10 seconds
You may not exceed the speed limit

q: While overtaking another vehicle, which statement is correct?
exp: Exceeding the speed limit when overtaking or passing is not permissible.

q: You are towing a vehicle with a tow-rope (not a tow-bar). What is your maximum speed?
exp: You may not tow with a tow-rope or chain faster than 30 km/h unless the vehicles are connected by a draw-bar or tow-bar.

q: What is the minimum following distance for a light motor vehicle in good conditions?
exp: Keep at least a 2-second following distance in a light motor vehicle or on a motorcycle; 3 seconds for heavy vehicles. Increase it in bad conditions.

q: What minimum following distance must the driver of a heavy motor vehicle keep?
exp: Heavy motor vehicles: at least 3 seconds. Light vehicles and motorcycles: at least 2 seconds.

opts.t: In rain, on slippery surfaces, in poor visibility, or when being followed too closely
Only when driving a heavy vehicle

q: When should you increase your following distance?
exp: Under adverse conditions such as rain, a slippery surface, poor visibility or when being followed too closely, increase your following distance.

q:
The distance it takes to stop a vehicle is …
(i) longer on a wet road than on a dry road
(ii) longer if the vehicle is travelling at a higher speed
(iii) longer if the vehicle is loaded
Select the correct combination.
exp: Wet roads, higher speeds and heavier loads all increase stopping distance.

q: Between which times must your headlamps be switched on?
exp: Headlamps, rear lamps and number-plate lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and at any other time when visibility is so poor that persons and vehicles are not clearly discernible at 150 m.

q: During the day you must switch on your headlamps when persons and vehicles are not clearly visible at a distance of …
exp: Lights must be on whenever, due to insufficient light or unfavourable weather, persons and vehicles are not clearly discernible at 150 metres.

opts.t: on the roadway in a rural area
within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the road
on the roadway, as long as the hazard lights are switched on

q: At night, your vehicle may be parked without its lights on if it is …
exp: The lighting requirement does not apply to a vehicle parked off the roadway, in a parking place demarcated by a road traffic sign, or within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the road. Hazard lights are not a substitute.

opts.t: At all times, day and night

q: When must the headlamp of a motorcycle be switched on?
exp: When riding a motorcycle on a public road, the headlamp must be lit at all times (day and night).

opts.t: on main (bright) beam so you can see further
switched off and parking lamps on

q: When following another vehicle at night, your headlamps should be …
exp: Dip your main beam for oncoming traffic and also when following another vehicle.

opts.t: driving very close behind the vehicle

q: A driver who wishes to overtake a vehicle ahead that is not in the left lane may make the other driver aware of their intention by …
exp: A driver who wants to overtake a vehicle ahead that is not in the left lane may give a visible signal by flashing the headlights.

opts.t: Any driver at night on rural roads
Emergency, police and traffic vehicles on official duty (and a few listed exceptions)

q: Who may use an adjustable spot lamp on their vehicle?
exp: Adjustable spot lamps are not allowed except on emergency, rescue, fire, police or traffic vehicles for official purposes, medical practitioners/vets on duty, and breakdown or essential-service vehicles at a scene.

opts.t: any vehicle displaying a yellow light
emergency vehicles sounding a siren and displaying emergency warning lights
any vehicle that hoots behind you

q: You must give an immediate right of way to …
exp: Drivers must give immediate right of way to all emergency vehicles sounding a siren and displaying emergency warning lights.

q: What colour warning light does a vehicle driven by a traffic officer on duty display?
exp: Fire, rescue, ambulance and emergency medical vehicles use red lights; traffic officers use blue; civil protection uses green.

q: What colour warning light is used by an ambulance?
exp: Ambulances, fire-fighting, rescue and emergency medical response vehicles use red warning lights.

q: What colour warning light is displayed by a vehicle engaged in civil protection?
exp: Vehicles used in civil protection show a green warning light.

opts.t: The driver and all passengers (3 years and older) where seatbelts are fitted

q: Who must wear a seatbelt while the vehicle is moving forward?
exp: The driver must ensure that all persons wear seatbelts. Rear-seat passengers must also wear fitted seatbelts. The seatbelt rule covers persons 3 years and older.

opts.t: A person between 3 and 14 years, unless taller than 1,5 m

q: For seatbelt purposes, who is regarded as a child?
exp: A child is a person aged 3 to 14 years, except if taller than 1,5 m, in which case they are regarded as an adult.

opts.t: a child who must sit in a child seat

q: A 12-year-old who is 1,6 m tall is regarded as …
exp: A person between 3 and 14 who is taller than 1,5 m is regarded as an adult, irrespective of age.

opts.t: uses an appropriate child restraint where available, otherwise wears a seatbelt
sits on an adult's lap in the front seat
sits in the front seat so the driver can see them

q: The driver must ensure that a child passenger aged 3 to 14 years …
exp: The driver must ensure a child uses an appropriate child restraint where available; if not, a seatbelt. If no seat with a seatbelt is available, the child must sit on the rear seat (if the vehicle has one). A child under 3 must always be in a child restraint (reg 213(6A), 2015).

opts.t: While reversing or moving in or out of a parking bay

q: When is it NOT compulsory to wear a seatbelt?
exp: It is not compulsory to wear a seatbelt while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area.

opts.t: the trip is shorter than 5 km
all other seats with seatbelts on that row are already occupied

q: An adult may sit in a seat on a row without a seatbelt only if …
exp: No adult may occupy a seat without a seatbelt on a row unless all other seats on that row fitted with seatbelts are already occupied.

q: Who is responsible for ensuring that all passengers wear seatbelts?
exp: The driver of a motor vehicle must ensure that all persons travelling in the vehicle wear a seatbelt.

opts.t: No, it is against the law

q: May passengers ride in a caravan being towed?
exp: It is against the law for passengers to ride in a caravan.

opts.t: half the height of the car measured from ground level

q: Goods on the roof of a motor car may not be higher (from the highest point of the roof) than …
exp: Goods on the roof of a motor car may not exceed half of the height of the car (measured from the ground). This does not apply to bicycles on the roof.

q: A load projecting more than 150 mm to the side or 300 mm to the rear must be marked during the day with …
exp: Such loads must be marked with a red flag (300 mm × 300 mm) by day and with retro-reflectors at night (white to the front, red to the rear).

q: At night, a load projecting beyond the rear of a vehicle must be marked with …
exp: At night, projecting loads must have white retro-reflectors to the front and red retro-reflectors to the rear.

q: A load on a light motor vehicle may not project beyond the rear of the vehicle by more than …
exp: Goods may not project more than 300 mm beyond the front or more than 1,8 m beyond the rear of a light or heavy motor vehicle.

q: A load on a motor vehicle may not project beyond the front of the vehicle by more than …
exp: Goods may not project more than 300 mm beyond the front end or 1,8 m beyond the rear end.

q: Goods loaded on a light motor vehicle may not make the overall width of the load more than …
exp: Goods may not project more than 1,25 m on either side of the centre line (max width 2,5 m); 1,3 m (max 2,6 m) for buses and goods vehicles with GVM over 12 000 kg.

opts.t: obscure the driver's view to the front or sides, or the view in the rear-view mirrors
touch the side of the load bay

q: Goods must be loaded on a vehicle so that they do NOT …
exp: Loads must not touch the road, obscure the driver's view to the front, sides or in the mirrors, and must be contained or securely fastened so they cannot fall off.

opts.t: 350 mm above the surface they sit on
900 mm above the surface they sit on

q: Persons carried seated on the back of a goods vehicle must be enclosed to a height of at least …
exp: The area must be enclosed to at least 350 mm above the surface where they are seated, or 900 mm above the surface where they are standing.

q: Persons carried standing on the back of a goods vehicle must be enclosed to a height of at least …
exp: 900 mm above the surface on which they stand (350 mm if seated).

opts.t: have a passenger in the front seat
allow any person, animal or object to be in a position that prevents you from having complete control of the vehicle

q: While driving, you may NOT …
exp: A driver may not permit any person, animal or object to occupy a position that prevents complete control of the vehicle, or allow anyone to hold or interfere with the steering or operating mechanism.

opts.t: on the roof if they hold on tightly
on the running board for short distances
only inside the vehicle in a proper position (never on the roof, step or running board)

q: While the vehicle is in motion, you may allow a person to ride …
exp: No person or animal may occupy the roof, any step or running board, or any other place on top of the vehicle while it is in motion.

q: You may allow part of your body to protrude from the vehicle while it is moving only …
exp: A driver may not allow any part of their body to protrude beyond the vehicle while it is moving, except to give a hand signal.

opts.t: on the right, at a safe distance
on whichever side has more space

q: You normally overtake a vehicle travelling in the same direction …
exp: Pass to the right at a safe distance, and do not move back to the left until you are safely clear of the vehicle you passed.

opts.t: the driver ahead is driving too slowly
the vehicle ahead is turning right (or has signalled to turn right) and it is safe
there is a gravel shoulder you can use

q: You may overtake on the left of another vehicle if …
exp: Passing on the left is allowed when it is safe and, for example, the vehicle ahead is turning right, or on a multi-lane one-way road, or on an urban road with two or more lanes in each direction, or when directed by a traffic officer.

opts.t: Yes, if the shoulder is tarred

q: May you overtake by driving on the shoulder or verge of the road?
exp: In no event may passing be done by driving on the shoulder of the roadway or the verge of a public road.

opts.t: the top of a rise, a curve or any place where your view is restricted

q: You may NOT overtake when approaching …
exp: Do not overtake when approaching the summit of a rise, a curve or any place where the view is restricted, unless you can do so without moving onto the right-hand side or the road is one-way.

opts.t: accelerate so it can pass quickly
keep as far left as safely possible and not accelerate until it has passed
move to the right to block it

q: When another vehicle is overtaking you, you must …
exp: Drive as near to the left edge as is safely possible and do not increase speed until the other vehicle has passed.

opts.t: overtake on the left if the left lane is empty
keep left and overtake on the right
stay in the right lane at all times

q: On a freeway you should …
exp: Vehicles must keep left and overtake to the right on any freeway.

opts.t: take due care for the safety of people getting on or off the bus
speed up to pass as quickly as possible

q: When passing a stationary bus, you must …
exp: A driver intending to pass a stationary bus must do so with due care for people approaching, leaving or who may approach or leave the bus.

opts.t: They may ride side by side at all times
They may not overtake another vehicle at the same time
They may overtake on the shoulder

q: Which rule applies to two or more motorcyclists riding in the same lane?
exp: Motorcyclists must ride in single file (except when overtaking another motorcycle), and two or more motorcyclists may not overtake another vehicle at the same time.

opts.t: on the left side of the roadway, not encroaching on the right half unless it can be done safely
in the centre of the road

q: On a road with a single roadway, you must drive …
exp: Drive on the left side of the roadway and do not encroach on the right half unless it can be done without obstructing or endangering other traffic, or as directed by a sign or officer.

opts.t: on any roadway that is less busy
on the left-hand roadway, unless a sign or traffic officer directs otherwise
on the right-hand roadway when overtaking

q: On a road divided into two or more roadways (a dual carriageway), you must drive …
exp: Where a public road is divided into two or more roadways, you must drive on the left-hand roadway unless directed or permitted otherwise.

opts.t: Between sunrise and sunset, on a road with one lane in each direction, while being overtaken, if it is safe and visibility is at least 150 m
At night when there are no street lights

q: When may you drive a light motor vehicle on the shoulder of the road?
exp: You may only use the shoulder during the day on a road with one lane in each direction, while being overtaken, when it is safe and when persons and vehicles are clearly visible at 150 m.

opts.t: only if you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic

q: You may change from one lane to another …
exp: On roads divided into lanes, you may not change lanes unless you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic. You must use your indicator.

opts.t: Yes, it is compulsory when turning and when changing lanes
No, only when turning at an intersection

q: Is it compulsory to use your direction indicator when changing lanes?
exp: It is compulsory to use direction indicators each time you turn left or right and when changing lanes.

opts.t: only if other traffic is close
in good time, clearly visible, and long enough to warn other road users

q: A driver who intends to stop or turn must give a signal …
exp: Signal in good time with a conspicuous signal visible to persons in front, behind or to the side, for long enough to warn them.

opts.t: only if it can be done in safety

q: You may let your vehicle travel backwards (reverse) …
exp: You may not cause your vehicle to travel backwards unless it can be done in safety.

opts.t: you can do so without interfering with moving traffic and with safety
you switch on your hazard lights

q: You want to move off from the side of the road where you were parked. You may only do so if …
exp: A driver may not drive from a parked position unless able to do so without interfering with moving traffic and with safety to themselves and others.

opts.t: if you signal and move slowly
only if it is clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance and you can do so safely
as long as you have right of way

q: You may cross or enter a public road …
exp: Do not cross a road unless it is clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance, and do not enter a road unless you can do so safely.

opts.t: to park in front of a shop
never – you may not drive, pull or push a vehicle on a sidewalk

q: You may drive on a sidewalk …
exp: No person may drive, pull or push a vehicle on a sidewalk.

opts.t: vehicles approaching from the right within the junction
all vehicles, including those behind you

q: Unless a road traffic sign or traffic officer directs otherwise, at a traffic circle (where traffic moves around an island) you must yield to …
exp: Unless signs or a traffic officer direct otherwise, yield to all vehicles approaching from your right within the traffic circle junction. At a mini-circle with a "yield at traffic circle" sign (R2.2), the vehicle that reaches its yield line first may proceed first.

q: At a 4-way stop, which vehicle may move off first?
exp: At a 3- or 4-way stop, the vehicle that stopped first moves off first. Proceed only when safe.

opts.t: with the front of your vehicle in line with the stop sign
with the rear of your vehicle in line with the stop sign

q: At a stop sign where there is no stop line, you must stop …
exp: Stop behind the stop line; if there is no line, the front of the vehicle must come to a standstill in line with the stop sign.

opts.t: may pass it carefully on the right
may not pass the stopped vehicle

q: Whenever a vehicle has stopped at a pedestrian crossing, the driver of any other vehicle …
exp: When a vehicle has stopped at a pedestrian crossing, other drivers may not pass it.

opts.t: yield right of way, slowing down or stopping if necessary

q: A pedestrian is crossing within a pedestrian crossing. You must …
exp: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing within a pedestrian crossing, slowing down or stopping if needed.

opts.t: wait in the middle of the road

q: The "red man" light signal flashes. Pedestrians who have already entered the roadway should …
exp: If the red man flashes, pedestrians who have not yet entered the roadway must wait for the green man; those already crossing must cross as quickly as possible.

q: You may not park within … of a fire hydrant (on the same side of the road).
exp: Do not park within 1,5 m on either side of a fire hydrant on the same side of the road.

q: In an urban area, you may not park within … of an intersection.
exp: In an urban area, do not park within 5 m of any intersection.

q: In an urban area, you may not park within … of the side from which you approach a pedestrian crossing.
exp: Do not park within 9 m of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing (and do not stop there either).

q: When parking on the roadway in an urban area, the outside of your left-hand wheels may not be more than … from the edge of the roadway.
exp: Do not park with the outside of any left-hand wheel more than 450 mm within the roadway.

q: In an urban area you may not park on a roadway that is less than … wide.
exp: Do not park on the roadway in an urban area where the roadway is less than 5,5 m wide.

q: Outside an urban area, you may not park on the roadway (excluding shoulders) or with any part of your vehicle within … of the edge of the roadway.
exp: Outside urban areas, do not park on any part of the roadway or with any part of the vehicle within 1 m of the edge of the roadway.

opts.t: Where your vehicle would obscure a road traffic sign
Off the road, on a property where the owner has given you permission

q: Where may you NOT park?
exp: You may not park where your vehicle would obscure a road traffic sign, nor where it encroaches on a sidewalk, blocks a vehicle entrance, or contravenes a sign.

opts.t: in a parking bay marked for you
on a traffic island, in a pedestrian mall or pedestrian lane
on the left side of a one-way street in a demarcated bay

q: You may NOT park …
exp: In an urban area you may not park on a traffic island or in a pedestrian mall or lane, or over the actuating mechanism of a traffic signal.

opts.t: set the parking brake (or otherwise prevent it from moving) and switch off the engine
leave the engine running so the battery does not go flat

q: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must …
exp: Do not leave a vehicle unattended without setting its brake, and do not let the engine run while the vehicle is stationary and unattended.

q: When parking in an angle-parking bay, the front of the vehicle may not be further than … from the kerb.
exp: In angle parking, park with the front not further than 150 mm from the kerb, and no part of the vehicle on or over the sidewalk.

q: You may not stop on any bridge or within … of a tunnel, subway or bridge.
exp: Do not stop in a tunnel, subway or on a bridge, or within 6 m of one (except to avoid an accident, obey an officer, or for a cause beyond your control).

q: You may not stop alongside or opposite another vehicle on a roadway that is less than … wide.
exp: Do not stop alongside or opposite another vehicle where the roadway is less than 9 m wide.

opts.t: On the left side of the roadway, facing the same direction as the traffic
On the right-hand side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic

q: Where may you NOT stop your vehicle?
exp: Do not stop on the right-hand side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic.

opts.t: at any time, except to avoid an accident, on an officer's direction or for a cause beyond your control

q: You may not stop within the railway reserve at a level crossing …
exp: Stopping is prohibited within the railway reserve at a level crossing.

q: You may not stop within … of the beginning or end of a part of the roadway where its normal width is constricted.
exp: Do not stop on, or within 6 m of the beginning or end of, any part of a roadway where its normal width has been constricted.

opts.t: whenever a pedestrian is on the sidewalk
at the request or signal of a person leading or driving animals such as cattle or horses on the road
when another driver flashes their lights at you

q: You MUST stop your vehicle …
exp: You must stop when directed by a sign or uniformed traffic officer, at the request of a person leading animals on the road, and when animals are crossing (wait until they have all crossed).

opts.t: hoot to chase them off the road
stop and wait until all the animals have crossed and it is safe to continue

q: Animals are crossing the road ahead of you. You must …
exp: When animals are seen crossing the road, stop and only move once all animals have crossed and it is safe.

q: You are legally required to stop when directed to do so by a traffic officer who is …
exp: You must stop when directed by a road traffic sign or by a traffic officer in uniform.

q: Which of the following vehicles is NOT legally required to carry an emergency warning sign (triangle)?
exp: Heavy motor vehicles, all goods vehicles, minibuses and buses must carry at least one emergency warning sign. Motor cars, ambulances and motorcycles are excluded, although carrying one in a car is still good practice.

q: When a motor vehicle is stationary on the roadway (for example after a breakdown), the emergency warning triangle must be placed at least … from the vehicle in the direction of approaching traffic.
exp: Place the triangle not less than 45 m from the vehicle in the direction from which traffic will approach, about as far from the edge as the centre of the vehicle, with the reflective side facing the traffic.

opts.t: The side with the manufacturer's name

q: Which side of the emergency warning triangle must face approaching traffic?
exp: The reflective side of the sign faces the direction from which traffic will approach.

opts.t: stop in the middle of the lane
stop as far left from the line as possible and switch on your emergency (hazard) lights
leave the vehicle and walk away without warning anyone

q: Your vehicle breaks down on a road with a left-edge line. You should …
exp: If your vehicle breaks down, stop as far left of the edge line as possible and switch on your emergency lights.

opts.t: move your vehicle off the road before checking anything

q: If you are involved in an accident, you must first …
exp: You must stop immediately, find out whether anyone is injured, assist injured persons, and determine the damage.

q: If you did not give your details to a traffic officer at the scene, you must report the accident at a police station within …
exp: If you did not furnish your details to a traffic officer at the scene, report the accident at a police station within 24 hours.

opts.t: take intoxicating liquor or drugs, except on a medical practitioner's instruction

q: After an accident, before you have reported it, you may not …
exp: Do not take intoxicating liquor or narcotic drugs (except on a doctor's instruction) before you have reported the accident.

opts.t: its position has been clearly marked on the road surface, or a traffic officer authorises it

q: After an accident in which a person was killed or injured, and the vehicles completely block the road, you may move a vehicle only if …
exp: A vehicle may not be moved unless its position has been clearly marked on the road surface or the removal is authorised by a traffic officer.

opts.t: your name and address, the owner's name and address, and the vehicle's registration number

q: At an accident, anyone with reasonable grounds may ask you for …
exp: You must give your name and address, the owner's name and address and the registration number to anyone with reasonable grounds to request them.

opts.t: The driver or owner of the vehicle
The first person to arrive at the scene

q: Who must give permission before a vehicle damaged in a collision may be removed from the scene (e.g. by a tow truck)?
exp: The driver or owner of a vehicle damaged in a collision must give permission before it can be removed from the scene.

q: What is the legal limit of alcohol in the blood for an ordinary (non-professional) driver?
exp: You may not drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0,05 g per 100 ml or more (0,02 g for professional drivers).

opts.t: Professional drivers may not drink at all for 24 hours before driving

q: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for a professional driver?
exp: For professional drivers (PDP holders) the limit is 0,02 g per 100 ml of blood.

opts.t: drive a vehicle, but you may sit in the driver's seat with the engine running
drive a vehicle or occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle while the engine is running
drive in an urban area, but you may drive on a rural road

q: Under the influence of alcohol or a narcotic drug, you may not …
exp: You may not drive, or occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle with the engine running, while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a narcotic drug.

q: What is the legal limit of alcohol in a breath specimen for an ordinary (non-professional) driver?
exp: Ordinary drivers: under 0,24 mg per 1 000 ml of breath (0,05 g per 100 ml of blood). Professional drivers: under 0,10 mg per 1 000 ml of breath (0,02 g per 100 ml of blood).
src: National Road Traffic Act s65 (breath limits are not in the 2012 manual)

q: What is the legal limit of alcohol in a breath specimen for a professional driver?
exp: Professional drivers: under 0,10 mg per 1 000 ml of breath (0,02 g per 100 ml of blood).
src: National Road Traffic Act s65 (breath limits are not in the 2012 manual)

opts.t: sits on an adult's lap with the adult's seatbelt around both of them
is seated in an appropriate child restraint
sits on the back seat without any restraint

q: A baby younger than 3 years is travelling in your private car. The law requires that the infant …
exp: Since 2015 (regulation 213(6A)) the driver must ensure that an infant under 3 years is seated in an appropriate child restraint. Minibuses, midibuses and buses carrying passengers for reward are exempt.
src: National Road Traffic Regulations reg 213(6A) (amendment after the 2012 manual)

opts.t: if you hold it in one hand and steer with the other
only while stopped at a red traffic light, holding it
only if you do not hold it in your hand or with any other part of your body (e.g. hands-free)

q: While driving, you may use a cellphone …
exp: No person may drive while holding a cellular phone or other communication device in one or both hands or with any other part of the body.

opts.t: A light motor vehicle towing a trailer
A motorcycle with an engine of 50 cm³ or less

q: Which of the following may NOT be used on a freeway?
exp: Prohibited on freeways: animal-drawn vehicles, pedal cycles, motorcycles of 50 cm³ or less (or electrically powered), motor quadrucycles, vehicles for disabled persons under 230 kg, and tractors (except for freeway work).

q: Which of the following is NOT allowed on a freeway?
exp: Pedal cycles may not be used on a freeway. Pedestrians may not be on a freeway under normal circumstances either.

opts.t: For a reason beyond your control, in a designated stopping area, or as directed by a sign or traffic officer

q: When may you stop on a freeway?
exp: You may only stop on a freeway as directed by a sign or officer, in an area reserved for stopping or parking, or for reasons beyond your control.

opts.t: Only for a reason beyond your control
Whenever your indicators are switched off

q: When may you give a hand signal while driving on a freeway?
exp: You may not give a hand signal on a freeway except for a reason beyond your control.

opts.t: speed up so it merges behind you
allow the vehicle to merge in front of you

q: You are driving on a freeway and a vehicle ahead wants to merge from an on-ramp. You must …
exp: A driver on the freeway who notices a vehicle in front wishing to merge from an on-ramp must allow it to merge in front of them.

opts.t: An animal may be on a freeway if it is tied up
You may not leave an animal anywhere from where it may stray onto a freeway
An animal may be left on the freeway verge

q: Which statement about animals and freeways is correct?
exp: No person may leave or allow an animal on a freeway, or leave an animal where it may stray onto a freeway.

q: What is the maximum length of a tow-rope, chain or tow-bar between two vehicles?
exp: You may not tow if the tow-rope, chain or tow-bar between the vehicles is longer than 3,5 m.

opts.t: Yes, if it has an engine over 125 cm³

q: May a motorcycle be used to tow another vehicle?
exp: No person shall use a motorcycle to tow another vehicle.

opts.t: the speed does not exceed 30 km/h
the tow-rope is shorter than 3,5 m

q: A towed vehicle (not a semi-trailer) may carry passengers only if …
exp: A towed vehicle conveying persons may not be towed faster than 30 km/h unless it is a semi-trailer.

opts.t: a person who holds a driving licence for that class of vehicle
nobody if a tow-bar is used

q: The steering of a vehicle being towed must be controlled by …
exp: The steering of the towed vehicle must be controlled by a person licensed to drive that class of vehicle.

q: A combination of motor vehicles may consist of a drawing vehicle and a maximum of …
exp: A combination is restricted to a drawing vehicle and a maximum of two trailers (or one other motor vehicle that is not a trailer).

opts.t: if it is a diesel vehicle

q: You may run the engine of your vehicle while fuel is being put into its tank …
exp: No person may allow the engine to run while petrol or other flammable fuel is being delivered into the tank.

opts.t: an emergency vehicle sounding a siren or bell
the vehicle with the most passengers

q: You must give an immediate and absolute right of way to …
exp: Drivers must give an immediate and absolute right of way to a vehicle sounding a device or bell (emergency vehicles).

opts.t: obey all road traffic signs and rules of the road
obey only the signs you agree with
obey signs only in urban areas

q: Unless a traffic officer orders you otherwise, you must …
exp: No person may disobey any road traffic sign or rule of the road unless ordered to do so by a traffic officer.

opts.t: Driving a vehicle without reasonable consideration for other road users
Driving at the general speed limit

q: Which of the following is an offence?
exp: No person may drive a vehicle on a public road without reasonable consideration for any other person using the road (inconsiderate driving).

q: Driving in a manner that wilfully disregards the safety of persons or property is …
exp: No person may drive recklessly or negligently or in a manner that wilfully disregards the safety of persons or property.

q: May you throw litter, oil or other refuse from your vehicle onto the road?
exp: No person may negligently or wilfully deposit fuel, oil, grease, flammable or offensive matter, ashes or refuse from a vehicle on or next to the road.

q: You may cause the wheels of your vehicle to spin or drag on the road surface …
exp: You may not cause a wheel to drag or spin on the road surface except in an emergency.

q: A vehicle left in the same place on a public road outside an urban area for more than … is deemed abandoned.
exp: Outside an urban area: 24 hours. Within an urban area: 7 days.

q: A vehicle left in the same place on a public road in an urban area for more than … is deemed abandoned.
exp: Within an urban area: 7 days. Outside an urban area: 24 hours.

q: You may operate a vehicle on a public road in a manner that causes excessive noise …
exp: No person shall operate a vehicle on a public road in a way that causes any excessive noise.

opts.t: keep at least one hand on the handlebars at all times
keep both feet on the ground when moving slowly
carry passengers in front of them

q: When riding a motorcycle, the rider must …
exp: A rider must keep at least one hand on the handlebars, sit astride the saddle, keep feet on the footrests, and keep all wheels in contact with the road.

q: To carry a passenger on a motorcycle, the engine capacity must exceed …
exp: A rider may not carry a passenger unless the engine exceeds 50 cm³ and the passenger sits in a side-car or astride on a pillion.

q: On which side of a motorcycle must a side-car be attached?
exp: A side-car must be attached to the left side of the motorcycle.

opts.t: The rider and any passenger (including a side-car passenger)

q: Who must wear a protective helmet on a motorcycle?
exp: The rider and passengers (including a side-car passenger) must wear a properly fitted helmet with the chin strap fastened. The rider must ensure passengers under 14 wear one.

opts.t: one brake acting on both wheels
two independent braking systems, one on the front wheel and one on the rear wheel

q: A motorcycle must have …
exp: A motorcycle must have two independent braking systems, one acting on the front wheel and one on the rear wheel(s).

q: How many persons may ride on a motorcycle (excluding a side-car)?
exp: Not more than two persons may ride on a motorcycle, excluding a person in a side-car.

opts.t: Two: one at the front and one at the rear

q: How many number plates must a motor car have?
exp: A motorcycle, motor tricycle or trailer has a plate at the back. All other motor vehicles have one at the back and one at the front.

q: A number plate must be fitted upright or within … of upright.
exp: A number plate must be affixed in an upright position or within 30 degrees of upright, not easily detachable, clearly legible and visible.

opts.t: while the vehicle is stationary and unattended

q: Your vehicle's engine must not run …
exp: No driver may allow the engine to run while the vehicle is stationary and unattended.

opts.t: its fuel tank, fuel pipes, wiring or battery are defective or exposed so that they are a source of danger
its battery is more than two years old

q: A motor vehicle may not be used on a public road if …
exp: Fuel tanks, carburettor and fuel pipes may not be defective or exposed so as to be dangerous; the tank must have an effective cap; wiring and battery must be properly installed, insulated and maintained.

q: The maximum overall width of a light motor vehicle is …
exp: Any vehicle (other than the listed buses and heavy goods vehicles) may not exceed an overall width of 2,5 m.

q: The maximum overall height of a vehicle (other than a double-deck bus), including its load, is …
exp: 4,3 m for vehicles in general; 4,65 m for a double-deck bus.

q: Apart from the listed exceptions (certain trailers, articulated vehicles, bus-trains and combinations), the maximum overall length of a vehicle is …
exp: Most single vehicles: 12,5 m. Articulated vehicle: 18,5 m. Combination or bus-train: 22 m.

q: What is the maximum overall length of a combination of motor vehicles?
exp: Any combination of motor vehicles: 22 m. Articulated vehicle: 18,5 m.

opts.t: apply only when the traffic light is broken
take precedence over any other traffic signal
may be ignored if the light is green

q: A traffic officer's hand signals …
exp: The traffic officer's signals take precedence over any other traffic signal. Follow the officer's directions strictly.

opts.t: stop until the "proceed" flag signal is shown

q: At road works, a flagman gives you the "stop" flag signal. You must …
exp: A stop flag signal means stop until the proceed flag signal is displayed. A warning flag means proceed slowly and be alert.

q:
You may NOT overtake a vehicle travelling in the same direction when you are approaching …
(i) the top of a rise
(ii) a curve
(iii) a place where dust or smoke limits your view of oncoming traffic
exp: Do not pass when approaching the summit of a rise, a curve, or any other place where the view is so restricted that passing could endanger oncoming traffic (unless you stay out of the right-hand side, or the road is one-way).

q:
You may pass another vehicle on its LEFT if it is safe and …
(i) the vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled that it will turn right
(ii) you are on a one-way road in an urban area that is wide enough for two or more lines of traffic
(iii) you drive on the shoulder of the road to do it
exp: Passing on the left is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning right, on suitable multi-lane urban roads, on one-way roads divided into lanes, or when a traffic officer directs it. You may never pass by driving on the shoulder or verge.

opts.t: Keep as far left as is safe and do not speed up until it has passed
Speed up so that it can get past you more quickly
Move towards the centre line so it cannot cut in too early

q: Another vehicle is overtaking you. Which statement is correct?
exp: When someone wishes to pass you, drive as near to the left edge of the roadway as is safe and do not accelerate until the other vehicle has passed.

q:
You are involved in an accident. You must …
(i) stop immediately
(ii) find out whether anyone is injured and help as far as you are able
(iii) leave the scene if the damage looks minor
exp: A driver involved in an accident must stop immediately, establish the injuries and help the injured as far as possible, establish the damage, and give their details to anyone with reasonable grounds to ask. Leaving the scene is not allowed.

q: After an accident, if you did not give your details to a traffic officer at the scene, you must report the accident at a police station within …
exp: If you did not give your and the owner's names and addresses and the vehicle registration number to a traffic officer at the scene, report the accident at a police station within 24 hours.

q:
You are disqualified from obtaining a learner's licence if you …
(i) suffer from uncontrolled epilepsy
(ii) are addicted to a drug with a narcotic effect
(iii) are deaf
exp: Uncontrolled epilepsy and drug or alcohol addiction disqualify you. The Act states that deafness is not, of itself, a disqualifying defect.

opts.t: A licence that has been suspended by a court, while the suspension is in force
Wearing glasses or contact lenses that correct your vision to the required standard

q: Which of the following does NOT disqualify you from holding a learner's licence?
exp: Defective vision (measured against the prescribed standard) disqualifies you, but vision corrected to the standard with glasses or lenses meets it. Uncontrolled diabetes and a suspended licence both disqualify you.

q:
Your headlamps, rear lamps and number-plate lamp must be switched on …
(i) between sunset and sunrise
(ii) during the day when rain makes it hard to see vehicles 150 m away
(iii) whenever you drive faster than 100 km/h
exp: Lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and at any other time when, because of poor light or bad weather, persons and vehicles are not clearly visible at 150 m. Speed has nothing to do with it.

q:
At night your parked car does NOT need its lamps switched on if it is parked …
(i) off the roadway of the public road
(ii) in a parking place demarcated by a road traffic sign
(iii) within 12 m of a lighted street lamp that lights up the road
exp: All three are exceptions to the rule that lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise.

opts.t: That the vehicle behind you has flashed its lights at you
That you can change lanes without obstructing or endangering other traffic
That you are driving faster than the traffic in the other lane

q: Before you change lanes, what must you be sure of?
exp: Signal in good time, check your mirrors and blind spot, and only move across when you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.

q:
You are about to change lanes. Put these in the correct order:
(i) check your mirrors and blind spot
(ii) give the signal in good time
(iii) move into the other lane when it is safe
exp: Observe first, signal in good time, check again (especially the blind spot), then change lanes only if it is safe. A signal alone never gives you the right to move over.
src: K53 observation routine; Rules of the Road 6.40 & 6.41

opts.t: 1 mm, with the tread pattern clearly visible across the whole tyre
0,5 mm on the front tyres only

q: What is the minimum tread depth of the tyres on a light motor vehicle?
exp: Tyres must show a clearly visible tread pattern across their breadth and around the entire circumference, with a tread depth of at least 1 mm.

opts.t: To tell the car in front that the traffic light has turned green
Only when it is necessary for safety reasons

q: When may you use the hooter of your vehicle?
exp: No person shall use a vehicle's hooter except when necessary on grounds of safety. It must be audible from 90 m, and hooters that play a tune may not be fitted to private vehicles.

opts.t: with a rope, at walking pace
by pushing it with another vehicle

q: The brakes of a vehicle no longer work. If it has to be towed, it should be towed …
exp: If the towed vehicle's brakes do not comply with the law, it may only be towed if it is connected to the towing vehicle by a draw bar or tow-bar. A rope or chain would let it run into the towing vehicle.

opts.t: Yes, if you lock the doors
Yes, for not more than 5 minutes
No, the engine may not run while the vehicle is unattended

q: May you leave your car on a public road with the engine running while you go into a shop?
exp: A driver may not leave a vehicle unattended with the engine running, and must make sure it cannot move (parking brake or gear).

q:
A vehicle left in the same place on a public road is regarded as abandoned after …
(i) 24 hours, outside an urban area
(ii) 7 days, inside an urban area
(iii) 30 days, anywhere
exp: A vehicle may be deemed abandoned if left in the same place for more than 24 hours on a public road outside an urban area, or more than 7 days inside an urban area.

q: Which control do you use to accelerate (increase the speed of) the vehicle?
exp: Number 10 is the accelerator. Pressing it increases engine speed and therefore road speed.

q: Which control is used to stop the vehicle?
exp: Number 9 is the (foot) brake – the service brake used to slow down and stop.

q: Which control is used to keep a parked vehicle stationary?
exp: Number 7 is the hand (parking) brake, used to keep the vehicle stationary after parking.

q: Which control is NOT found in a vehicle with an automatic gearbox?
exp: Automatic vehicles do not have a clutch (number 8). They still have a gear selector (6) and an accelerator (10).

q: In a vehicle with a manual gearbox, which controls do you use to change gears?
exp: To change gear you depress the clutch (8) and move the gear lever (6).

q: Which control assists the driver when engaging or disengaging a gear?
exp: The clutch (8) disconnects the engine from the gearbox so that a gear can be engaged or disengaged.

q: Which control is used to change the direction of the vehicle?
exp: The steering wheel (4) changes the direction of the vehicle. The indicator (5) only signals your intention.

q: Which control do you use to tell other road users that you intend to turn left or right?
exp: Number 5 is the indicator switch. It signals your intention to turn or change direction.

q: Which control is used to clean the front windscreen, for example when driving in the rain?
exp: Number 2 is the windscreen wiper.

q: Which control would you use to see what is on the right-hand rear side of your vehicle?
exp: Number 3 is the left and right (side) rear-view mirrors. The right-hand mirror shows the right-rear side.

q: Which control is used to alert other road users in order to avoid a collision?
exp: Number 11 is the horn (hooter). It may only be used when necessary for safety.
src: Vehicle Controls Manual 2.6; Rules of the Road 6.15

q: Which control should you use (check) before applying the brake to slow down or stop?
exp: Check the centre rear-view mirror (1) before braking so that you know what traffic is behind you.

q: Which control should you use (check) before changing the speed of the vehicle?
exp: Before changing speed, first check the rear-view mirror (1) to be aware of the traffic behind you.

q: Which control is used to prevent the engine from stalling just before the vehicle comes to a complete standstill?
exp: Depress the clutch (8) just before you stop so that the engine does not stall.

q: Which control(s) are used to see what is to the rear and sides of the vehicle?
exp: The centre mirror (1) shows traffic directly behind; the side mirrors (3) show the rear and sides.

q: Which control do you use to select a gear?
exp: Number 6 is the gear lever.

q: Which control must be used to keep the vehicle stationary when parking and leaving it unattended?
exp: The hand (parking) brake (7) must be set before leaving a vehicle unattended.
src: Vehicle Controls Manual 2.6; Rules of the Road 6.49

q: Which control is used to stop the vehicle in an emergency?
exp: The foot brake (9) is used to stop in an emergency.

q: When you stop on a steep incline and want to prevent the vehicle from rolling backwards, which control do you use?
exp: The hand brake (7) holds the vehicle on an incline.

q: When you intend to change direction, which controls are used?
exp: Check the mirrors (1 and 3) and signal with the indicator (5) before changing direction.

q: Which controls must you use when there is a sharp turn in the road?
exp: For a sharp turn you check your mirrors (1 and 3), brake to slow down (9), change down a gear (clutch 8 and gear lever 6), steer (4) and use the accelerator (10). The manual gives 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 in section 2.11 (section 2.6 leaves out 3). Either way, the other two options are clearly wrong.

q: Which of the following is a foot control?
exp: The brake (9) is a foot pedal. The hand brake (7) and indicator (5) are operated by hand.

q: Which of the following is NOT a hand control?
exp: The accelerator (10) is operated with your foot.

q: Control number 4 is the …
exp: Number 4 is the steering wheel.

q: Control number 1 is the …
exp: Number 1 is the centre (interior) rear-view mirror.

q: Control number 8 is used to …
exp: Number 8 is the clutch, used together with the gear lever to change gears.

q: Control number 6 is the …
exp: Number 6 is the gear lever.

q: Control number 11 is the …
exp: Number 11, in the middle of the steering wheel, is the horn.

q: Which control is used to increase and decrease the speed of the vehicle?
exp: The accelerator (10) controls engine speed: press to go faster, ease off to slow down.

q: Which control is used to monitor traffic to the rear?
exp: The side rear-view mirrors (3) (together with the centre mirror, 1) are used to monitor traffic behind you.

q:
When control number 9 is used, the distance it takes to stop the vehicle is …
(i) longer on a wet road than on a dry road
(ii) longer if the vehicle is travelling at a higher speed
(iii) longer if the vehicle is loaded
Select the correct combination.
exp: All three are correct: wet roads, higher speeds and heavier loads all increase stopping distance.

q: You are driving a vehicle with an automatic gearbox. Which control is used to select Drive, Neutral, Reverse or Park?
exp: In an automatic vehicle number 6 is the gear selector. It works differently from a manual gear lever, and there is no clutch.

q: Which control should you check before moving off from the side of the road?
exp: Before moving off you must be able to do so safely without interfering with moving traffic, so check your mirrors (3 and 1) and blind spot.
src: Vehicle Controls Manual 2.5; Rules of the Road 6.49

q: Which control must be in good working order and audible from 90 m?
exp: A light motor vehicle must have a hooter (11) in good working order that is clearly audible from 90 metres.

q: Which controls are used in combination to change from 3rd gear to 2nd gear?
exp: To change from one gear to another (for example from 3rd to 2nd) you depress the clutch (8) and move the gear lever (6).

q: Where a vehicle has a foot-operated parking brake (e.g. some Mercedes-Benz models), which control does it replace?
exp: The manual notes that some vehicles have the parking (hand) brake, number 7, as a foot-operated control.

opts.t: Front brake, rear brake and engine brake
Service brake, parking brake and emergency brake
Foot brake, clutch and gearbox brake

q: A light motor vehicle must have which three brakes (two may be the same brake)?
exp: Every light and heavy motor vehicle must have a service brake, a parking brake and an emergency brake. The parking and emergency brake may be one and the same.

opts.t: the brake, normally a footbrake, used in the ordinary course of events to slow down or stop
the hand brake used to keep a vehicle stationary
any brake other than the footbrake that can stop the vehicle

q: The "service brake" is …
exp: The service brake is normally the footbrake. The parking brake is normally the hand brake. An emergency brake is a brake other than the service brake that can stop the vehicle.

opts.t: the brake used to slow down in normal traffic
a brake, normally a hand brake, used to keep the vehicle stationary

q: The parking brake of a vehicle is …
exp: The parking brake is normally the hand brake and is used to keep a vehicle stationary.

q: A vehicle designed for or capable of reaching what speed must be fitted with a working speedometer?
exp: A motor vehicle that can reach 60 km/h or more must have a speedometer in good working order.

opts.t: One, which wipes the windscreen directly in front of the driver

q: How many windscreen wipers must at least be fitted to a light motor vehicle with a windscreen?
exp: At least one windscreen wiper must be fitted that wipes the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver continuously, evenly and adequately.

opts.t: an exterior rear-view mirror on the driver's side and an interior rear-view mirror
an exterior rear-view mirror on the passenger side only

q: A motor car must be fitted with …
exp: A motor car, minibus, bus or goods vehicle must have an exterior mirror on the driving side and an interior mirror. If the interior mirror does not give a clear view to the rear, an extra exterior mirror on the other side must be fitted instead.

q: The visible light transmittance through the windscreen of a light motor vehicle must be at least …
exp: The windscreen must be of safety glass, give sufficient visibility, and have a visible light transmittance of at least 70%.

q: A direction indicator on a light motor vehicle, when in use, must be clearly visible in normal daylight at a distance of …
exp: Indicators must show an intermittently flashing light clearly visible in normal daylight at 30 metres.

q: The light from a stop lamp must be visible in normal sunlight at a distance of at least …
exp: Stop lamps must emit red light brighter than the rear lamps and be visible in normal sunlight at 30 metres.

q: What colour light may a direction indicator show to the rear?
exp: Indicators must show white, yellow or amber to the front, and yellow, amber or red to the rear.

q: The number-plate lamp must make every letter and figure on the plate visible from a distance of …
exp: At least one number-plate lamp must illuminate the rear plate so that it is legible from 20 metres.

opts.t: When there is oncoming traffic and when following another vehicle
Only when an oncoming driver flashes their lights

q: When must the main (bright) beam of your headlamps be dipped?
exp: Dip your main beam for oncoming traffic as well as when following another vehicle so that you do not dazzle other drivers.

q: A properly adjusted main (bright) beam must let you see a person, vehicle or substantial object at a distance of at least …
exp: Main beam: at least 100 m. Dipped beam: at least 45 m.

q: A properly adjusted dipped beam must let you see a person, vehicle or substantial object at a distance of at least …
exp: Dipped beam: at least 45 m. Main beam: at least 100 m.

opts.t: fog, mist, snow, dust or smoke

q: You may use your fog lamps only when visibility is poor because of …
exp: No vehicle may be driven with fog lamps lit except in poor visibility caused by snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke.

opts.t: Yes, in urban areas at night
Yes, if the street lights are on
No, a moving vehicle may not be driven with only its parking lamps lit

q: May you drive with only your parking lamps switched on?
exp: A vehicle may not be driven on a public road with only the parking lamps lighted while it is in motion.

q: What is the minimum tread depth of the tyres of a light motor vehicle?
exp: Tyres must have a clearly visible tread pattern across the breadth and around the whole circumference, at least 1 mm deep.

opts.t: It may be used to greet friends
It may only be used when necessary on the grounds of safety
It may be fitted with a musical tune in a private vehicle

q: Which statement about the hooter (horn) is correct?
exp: The hooter may only be used when necessary for safety. Sirens or tune-playing warning devices may not be used in private vehicles.

q: The light emitted by a vehicle's rear lamps must be …
exp: Rear lamps must emit a red light to the rear.

opts.t: None if it has rear lamps

q: How many red retro-reflectors must be fitted to the rear of a light motor vehicle?
exp: A light motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors on the rear, one on each side.

q: The maximum turning radius allowed for a motor vehicle used on a public road is …
exp: A motor vehicle may not be used on a public road if its turning radius exceeds 13,1 metres.

opts.t: It is legal to remove the silencer if the vehicle is roadworthy
The vehicle must have an efficient silencer, and exhaust gas must not leak into the passenger compartment
Dense smoke is acceptable if the engine is new

q: Which statement about the exhaust system is correct?
exp: A vehicle must have an efficient exhaust silencer, may not emit smoke so dense that it is a nuisance or obscures vision, and exhaust gas may not leak into the cab or passenger compartment.

opts.t: Between sunset and sunrise, and whenever people and vehicles are not clearly visible at 150 metres

q: When should a vehicle's headlamps, rear lamps and number-plate lamp be switched on?
exp: These lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise and at any other time when, because of insufficient light or bad weather, persons and vehicles are not clearly discernible at 150 metres.

q: Which number on the diagram is NOT found in a vehicle with an automatic gearbox?
exp: Number 8 is the clutch. An automatic gearbox has no clutch pedal; it still has a gear selector (6) and a brake (9).

q: Which controls do you use to select a gear in a vehicle with a manual gearbox?
exp: Depress the clutch (8) and move the gear lever (6).

q: In a vehicle with an automatic gearbox, which control do you use to stop the vehicle?
exp: Number 9 is the brake (service brake). In an automatic there are only two pedals: brake (9) and accelerator (10).

q: What is the ordinary shape of a regulatory sign?
exp: Regulatory signs are usually round; warning signs triangular; guidance signs rectangular.

q: What is the ordinary shape of a warning sign?
exp: Warning signs are triangular and alert you in time to dangerous conditions on or next to the road.

opts.t: The octagonal stop sign, the triangular yield sign and the diamond-shaped pedestrian priority sign
Keep left and keep right signs

q: Which regulatory signs are exceptions to the usual round shape?
exp: Regulatory signs are usually round. Exceptions: stop (octagon), yield (triangle) and pedestrian priority (diamond).

opts.t: a temporary sign, indicating a change in normal circumstances (e.g. road works)
only advisory and need not be obeyed

q: A road sign with a yellow background is …
exp: Yellow-background signs are temporary signs, used at road works, collision scenes and temporary traffic control. They must still be obeyed.

q: A road traffic sign number that begins with the letter "T" (e.g. TR201) indicates …
exp: A number beginning with T indicates a temporary sign.

opts.t: To regulate and control road users' actions by prohibiting or commanding certain actions

q: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
exp: Regulatory signs prohibit or command; disobeying them is an offence punishable by a fine, imprisonment or both.

opts.t: allowed if no sign is present
an offence, just like disobeying a regulatory sign

q: Failure to obey a regulatory road marking is …
exp: As with regulatory signs, it is an offence to disregard regulatory markings.

opts.t: To command you to do something
To alert you in time to dangerous conditions on or next to the road
To show you the route to a town

q: What is the purpose of warning signs?
exp: Warning signs alert road users in time to dangerous conditions.

opts.t: To help you navigate, e.g. by giving early indication of routes and destinations

q: What is the purpose of guidance signs?
exp: Guidance signs help you navigate by giving early indications that you will soon reach a particular place.

opts.t: The restriction shown by the symbol ends from here
The sign is out of order

q: What does a red cross (diagonal bars) over a regulatory sign symbol mean, as in the de-restriction signs (R600)?
exp: De-restriction signs cancel a restriction: from there you no longer need to comply with the sign shown without the cross.

opts.t: Anywhere you can see cross traffic
With the front of your vehicle in line with the sign

q: You approach this sign and there is no stop line. Where must you stop?
exp: Stop behind the stop line; where there is none, the front of the vehicle must stop in line with the stop sign.

opts.t: The vehicle approaching from the right

q: You and three other vehicles arrive at this intersection. Which vehicle may proceed first?
exp: At a 4-way stop, the vehicle that stopped first moves off first, when it is safe.

opts.t: You may turn left without stopping, but must yield to all traffic close enough to be a hazard

q: You want to turn left at this sign. What must you do?
exp: The stop/yield sign lets traffic turning left proceed without stopping if it can be done without interfering with cross traffic. Straight-through traffic must stop.

opts.t: Proceed; the sign applies only to left-turning traffic

q: You want to go straight on at this sign. What must you do?
exp: If you intend to carry straight on, bring your vehicle to a standstill behind the stop line.

opts.t: The driver who reaches their yield line first

q: At a mini-circle with this sign, who may proceed first?
exp: Yield to vehicles already in the circle or that will cross their yield line before you cross yours; the driver who reaches the yield line first proceeds first.

opts.t: Yes, as at a normal intersection, signal in time
No, signalling is not used at circles

q: At a mini-circle controlled by this sign, must you signal your intended direction?
exp: At a mini circle you must, as at a normal intersection, signal in time in which direction you want to turn.

opts.t: Only emergency, loading/off-loading and maintenance vehicles, at max 15 km/h

q: Which vehicles may enter an area marked with this sign, and at what maximum speed?
exp: Pedestrian priority areas limit other traffic to emergency vehicles, delivery (loading/off-loading) and maintenance vehicles, driving at a maximum of 15 km/h and giving way to pedestrians.

opts.t: At the end of a one-way street or off-ramp
At the beginning of a freeway

q: Where would you usually find this sign?
exp: No entry signs are usually found at the end of a one-way street, at the end of an off-ramp or where a two-way road changes to one-way.

opts.t: Stop and wait for a traffic officer
Proceed with caution if it is safe

q: At road works, a worker turns this STOP/GO sign so that the GO side faces you. What must you do?
exp: STOP/GO signs are two signs mounted back to back: stop if STOP faces you; proceed with caution when GO is shown.

opts.t: Do not drive slower than 50 km/h

q: What does this sign require of you?
exp: A blue round sign with a number is a minimum speed sign: do not drive slower than the speed shown.

opts.t: Do not drive slower than 60 km/h

q: What does this sign require of you?
exp: A red-bordered round sign with a number is a speed limit: do not exceed it. The limit applies from the sign.

opts.t: Turn left at the next intersection
Pass to the left of the obstruction (e.g. traffic island)
Keep to the left lane on a freeway

q: What must you do at this sign?
exp: Keep left signs are found at obstructions such as traffic islands: pass on the side indicated.

q: At a roundabout with this sign, in which direction must you travel?
exp: Proceed clockwise, yielding to vehicles approaching from the right within the roundabout.

opts.t: To show a toll plaza 1 km ahead
To give you a last opportunity to take an alternative route, or proceed and pay toll

q: What is the purpose of this sign?
exp: The pay toll sign gives you a last chance to take an alternative route or proceed and pay.

opts.t: Switch on your headlights in the dipped position

q: What must you do at this sign?
exp: Switch your lights on in the dip position so you can see and be seen (often before tunnels).

opts.t: Use a part of the road not indicated by this sign

q: You are driving a light motor vehicle with a GVM of 1 500 kg. This sign applies to the left lane. What must you do?
exp: Vehicles exceeding the indicated mass must use the part of the road indicated; lighter vehicles must use another part of the road.

opts.t: Yes, any light vehicle may use it
No, only motor cars may use it

q: You are driving a minibus. May you use a lane marked with this sign?
exp: Motor cars only: you may use such a road only when the sign depicting your type of vehicle is displayed.

opts.t: Yes – parking is prohibited, but a brief stop to load or off-load is not parking
Only if you switch on your hazard lights for 5 minutes

q: At this sign, may you stop briefly to drop off a passenger?
exp: This is the parking prohibited sign. "Park" means stationary for longer than needed to load or off-load persons or goods, so a brief stop is allowed. The "S" sign prohibits stopping.
src: Road Traffic Signs 3.3 (R216); Rules of the Road definitions

opts.t: To drop off a passenger quickly
Only to obey a traffic light or officer, or to avoid a collision

q: When may you stop where this sign is displayed?
exp: Stopping prohibited: do not stop unless to obey a traffic light or traffic officer, or to avoid a collision.

q: For how far does this sign normally apply?
exp: Do not overtake any vehicle for the next 500 m.

opts.t: Drivers of heavy (goods) vehicles, who may not overtake other heavy vehicles
All drivers, who may not overtake trucks
Truck drivers, who may not overtake light vehicles

q: Who is affected by this sign?
exp: R215: if you drive a heavy motor vehicle, do not overtake another heavy vehicle for the next 500 m.

q: For what distance after this sign may a driver not pick up passengers?
exp: Hitch-hiking prohibited: pedestrians may not try to be picked up, and drivers may not pick up passengers for the next 500 m.

q: For how far after this sign may you not use your hooter?
exp: Excessive noise prohibited (often near hospitals): do not use your hooter for 100 m after the sign.

q: At this sign, which movements are allowed?
exp: Where a left-turn prohibition is displayed, you may proceed straight or turn right.

q: At this sign, which movements are allowed?
exp: Where a right-turn prohibition is displayed, you may proceed straight or turn left.

opts.t: The road ahead is 4,42 m wide
Vehicles (including their load) higher than 4,42 m may not proceed

q: What does this sign mean?
exp: Height limit: if your vehicle or load is higher than the height in metres, use another road.

opts.t: Vehicles with a GVM or GCM exceeding 12 t may not use the road

q: What does this sign mean?
exp: Mass limit: if your vehicle's GVM or GCM exceeds the mass shown, use another road.

opts.t: assume there will be no pedestrians

q: Where pedestrians are prohibited by this sign, a driver should …
exp: Despite the prohibition you must still look out for pedestrians.

opts.t: Leave the freeway at the first exit

q: You are riding a motorcycle on a freeway and see this sign. What must you do?
exp: Motorcycles prohibited: on a freeway, motorcyclists must leave at the first exit.

opts.t: It is only a recommended speed
It is a temporary speed limit, e.g. at road works, which you must obey
It applies only to heavy vehicles

q: What does the yellow background of this sign tell you?
exp: A yellow background means a temporary sign. It must still be obeyed.

opts.t: No, the stop is reserved for buses of the indicated operator
Yes, if no bus is in sight

q: You are driving a car. May you stop here to drop off a passenger?
exp: Do not stop to pick up or drop off passengers if you are not driving the vehicle the stop is reserved for.

opts.t: A freeway begins and the freeway rules apply from here

q: What does this sign indicate?
exp: Dual-carriageway freeway begins: all freeway rules apply from the sign.

q: What is the speed limit in an area marked with this sign?
exp: A woonerf limits speed to 30 km/h, gives pedestrians right of way and prohibits through traffic.

q: In the area marked with this sign, who has right of way?
exp: In a woonerf you must yield to pedestrians and look out for children playing in the street.

opts.t: U-turns are prohibited during the day only
U-turns are prohibited at night only
U-turns are prohibited at all times

q: This plate is displayed below a no-U-turn sign. What does it mean?
exp: The night-time plate (R512) means the regulatory sign above it applies only during night time.

opts.t: Pay the parking fee and display the receipt in or on your vehicle

q: What must you do where this plate is displayed below a parking sign?
exp: Pay and display: pay the parking fee and display the receipt.

opts.t: You are approaching a crossroad where you have right of way (the thicker line)
You must yield to cross traffic

q: What does this sign tell you?
exp: The thicker leg of the cross indicates the road with priority. Here your road has priority, but be ready to stop if cross-traffic does not yield.

opts.t: You have right of way at the crossroad ahead
You are approaching a crossroad where you must yield to cross-traffic

q: What does this sign tell you?
exp: The thicker horizontal line indicates the crossing road has priority; you must yield to traffic from the left and right.

q: At a traffic circle with no other signs or markings telling you who has right of way, you must yield to traffic …
