exp: If there is no indication, give way to traffic approaching from the right. Vehicles within a traffic circle have right of way.

opts.t: There will be exactly two curves
There could be any number of curves after the first one, without further warning
The road becomes straight after 100 m

q: What should you keep in mind after passing this sign?
exp: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves; there could be any number after the first one without further warning.

opts.t: The one-way road you are on will soon carry two-way traffic

q: What does this sign warn you of?
exp: Two-way traffic ahead: be careful when overtaking because of oncoming vehicles.

q: For approximately what distance should you look out for pedestrians after this sign?
exp: Pedestrians may be crossing the road for the next 2 km. The same applies to cyclists, domestic and wild animals and slippery road signs.

q: A vehicle has stopped at the pedestrian crossing ahead warned of by this sign. You may …
exp: Slow down and stop for pedestrians waiting; do not overtake vehicles that have stopped at the pedestrian crossing.

opts.t: On the railway line, so the train driver can see you
In time, but not within the railway crossing reserve

q: A train is approaching as you near this crossing. Where must you stop?
exp: Slow down and look left and right; if a train is approaching, stop in time but not within the railway reserve.

q: At this railway crossing there is no stop line or stop sign. A train is approaching. How close to the nearest rail may you stop?
exp: If there is no stop line or sign, stop no closer than 3 m from the nearest track, and not on the track or in the railway reserve.

opts.t: Slow down and switch your headlights on (dipped)

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
exp: Tunnel ahead: slow down and switch on your headlights in the dipped position.

q: There is oncoming traffic as you approach this sign. How far from the structure should you stop to yield?
exp: Slow down, stop at least 6 m from the structure and yield to the other vehicle.

opts.t: Steering will be heavier and stopping distances shorter
Steering will be lighter, the vehicle will skid more easily and need a longer stopping distance

q: After this sign, how will your vehicle behave compared to a tarred road?
exp: On gravel, steering is lighter, vehicles skid more easily and need a longer stopping distance.

opts.t: Stop to look, in case you can help, even if help is there
Slow down, be ready to stop, and do not stop out of curiosity if enough help is present
Speed up to clear the area quickly

q: What should you do when passing a collision scene warned of by this sign?
exp: Slow down, watch for someone directing traffic and be ready to stop. If enough professional help is present, do not stop out of curiosity.

opts.t: follow the vehicle in front closely

q: You arrive at the drift warned of by this sign and do not know how deep the water is. You should …
exp: If it is not known how deep the water is, stop. If passable, drive through slowly.

q: What should you avoid after this sign?
exp: Slow down, since sudden braking or harsh steering could cause skidding sooner than usual.

opts.t: Do not get a fright and do not brake suddenly if an aircraft passes low
Stop and wait for the aircraft to land

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
exp: Low-flying aircraft: expect sudden aircraft noise near the road; do not get frightened or brake suddenly.

opts.t: Police are on duty ahead (e.g. roadblock or collision scene); be ready to stop

q: What does a blue flashing light shown on this temporary sign indicate?
exp: Temporary police flashing light: be ready to stop at the stop sign that follows or on demand of a police officer.

opts.t: Proceed at normal speed; you have right of way
Slow down, yield to other traffic and be ready to stop
Stop and wait until the lights work again

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
exp: The traffic signal ahead is out of order: slow down, yield and be ready to stop; look out for a traffic officer or stop sign.

opts.t: The road ahead curves sharply in the direction the chevron points (left)

q: What does this chevron sign tell you?
exp: Sharp curve chevrons warn that the road curves suddenly; slow down to take the curve safely.
src: Road Traffic Signs 4.3 (sharp curve chevron, W405 left)

opts.t: Avoid driving or stopping on the shoulder
Drive on the shoulder to let others pass

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
exp: Soft shoulder: do not drive or stop on the shoulder; if unavoidable, slow down as much as possible because the vehicle will pull towards the shoulder.

opts.t: It is the speed limit for this road
If you maintain this recommended speed, the next traffic signals should be green

q: What does the speed shown on this sign mean?
exp: Co-ordinated traffic signals: the speed is a recommendation, not a speed limit.

opts.t: Wait until your own signal is green
Move off with the oncoming traffic
Turn right, since the oncoming traffic has priority

q: At an intersection with this sign, oncoming traffic gets a green light while your light stays red. What should you do?
exp: Multi-phase signals do not follow the normal sequence. Do not move off when approaching traffic moves; wait for your green.

opts.t: Yield to traffic from the right
You have the right of way at the intersection ahead

q: What does this sign tell you?
exp: Right-of-way sign: do not slow down unnecessarily, but make sure other traffic will yield.

q: Countdown signs (IN3, IN2, IN1) before a freeway exit indicate the exit is approximately …
exp: Countdown signs indicate an exit about 300 m, 200 m and 100 m ahead.

q: The pre-advance exit direction sign on a freeway is placed approximately how far before an off-ramp?
exp: Pre-advance exit direction (GA1): about 2 km before the off-ramp. Advance exit (GA2): about 1 km. Supplementary exit: about 500 m.

q: By the time you pass the supplementary exit direction sign (about 500 m before the off-ramp) and want to leave the freeway, you should be …
exp: By the supplementary exit sign you should already be in the extreme left-hand lane.

q: The gore exit sign is placed between the off-ramp and the continuing freeway. If you want to leave the freeway, you pass it …
exp: Pass on the left of the gore sign to leave the freeway, and on the right to stay on it.

opts.t: drive straight into the arrestor bed

q: If the brakes of your vehicle fail on a steep descent with an arrestor bed, you should …
exp: Arrestor beds are gravel areas that stop vehicles whose brakes have failed; drive straight into it.

opts.t: confirm the destinations and distances ahead so you can plan stops for fuel and rest

q: A confirmation sign on a freeway is placed about 750 m after entering the freeway. Its purpose is to …
exp: Confirmation signs (GA7) confirm the destinations and distances.

opts.t: It has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop with your vehicle behind the line
Stop only if a pedestrian is present

q: You approach this marking and there is no stop sign. What does it mean?
exp: A stop line without a stop sign has the same meaning as a stop sign.

opts.t: Yield: give way to anyone who crosses or wants to cross your path, even if there is no yield sign

q: What does this road marking (broken transverse line with a triangle) mean?
exp: The yield line indicates you must give priority to all who cross in front of you, even without a yield sign.

opts.t: A yield sign or yield line ahead

q: What does this triangle marking painted in your lane warn you of?
exp: Yield control ahead (WM5) warns that there is a yield sign ahead.

opts.t: You may cross it to overtake when the road is clear
You may not drive with any part of your vehicle to the right of it, except to enter or leave an entrance on the other side or to pass a stationary obstruction, when safe

q: You are driving the blue car. What does the solid white centre line (no-overtaking line) mean?
exp: RM1: do not cross except to gain direct access to or from an entrance on the other side, or to pass a stationary obstruction – and only when safe.

opts.t: To turn into a driveway on the right
Only to drive around a stationary vehicle or obstruction in the road

q: When may you cross these double solid lines (no-crossing lines)?
exp: RM2: you may under no circumstances cross, except to drive around a stationary vehicle or obstruction.

opts.t: Yes, when it is safe, because the line on your side is broken
Only if the oncoming lane has a broken line on its side

q: You are driving the blue car. On your side of the centre markings is a broken line next to a solid line. May you cross to overtake?
exp: A solid line applies to traffic on the side where it is nearest. With a broken line on your side, you may cross when it is safe; traffic on the solid-line side may not cross.
src: National Road Traffic Regulations road-marking rules (not spelled out in the 2012 learner manual)

opts.t: All traffic is moving in your direction
Vehicles on the other side are moving in the opposite direction
You may not cross it at any time

q: What does this broken centre line (dividing line) warn you of?
exp: Dividing lines warn that vehicles on the other side are moving in the opposite direction; be alert for vehicles moving onto your side.

opts.t: You are on a part of the road with traffic moving in the same direction; drive in the centre of your lane

q: What do these broken lane lines indicate?
exp: Lane lines (GM1) show traffic in the same direction; drive in the centre of your demarcated lane.

opts.t: No parking, but you may stop briefly
No stopping, except in an emergency

q: What does a red line along the edge of the road mean?
exp: Red no-stopping lines (RM12): except in an emergency, do not stop.

opts.t: You may stop briefly, but may not park
You may not stop at all

q: What does a yellow no-parking line (RM13) painted along the kerb mean?
exp: No parking line (RM13): you may stop for short periods but may not park.

opts.t: You may wait inside the box when turning right
Do not stop inside the box; only enter if you can drive through
Parking is allowed in the box at night

q: What does this yellow box junction marking mean?
exp: Box junction (RM10): do not stop in the demarcated box; make sure you can drive through before entering.

opts.t: Only on the orders of a traffic or police officer, to avoid a collision, or in an emergency
At night when the road is empty

q: When may you drive over a painted island?
exp: Painted island (RM5): do not stop, park or drive over it except on an officer's orders, to avoid a collision or in an emergency.

opts.t: Give priority to pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross by slowing down or stopping
Stop only if a traffic light is red

q: What must you do at this marking?
exp: Pedestrian crossing lines: give pedestrians priority by slowing down or stopping.

opts.t: A break (intersection or off-ramp) ahead; a lane with this line may soon turn off the road

q: What do these short, closely spaced broken lines (continuity lines) warn you of?
exp: Continuity lines (WM2) warn of a break in the road; if your lane has a line on one side, it will soon turn off. Yield to traffic changing lanes.

opts.t: Yes, if no bus is in sight
No, it is reserved for buses during those times

q: You are driving a car. May you drive in a lane marked like this during the times shown on the bus lane sign?
exp: Bus lane marking (RM9): if you are not driving a bus, do not drive in the lane during the times on the sign.

opts.t: at any time when traffic is slow
during the day, while being overtaken, if safe, and when visibility is at least 150 m
at night when the road is empty

q: The left-edge line of the road may be crossed to drive on the shoulder only …
exp: You may drive left of the left-edge line only while being overtaken, if safe, during daytime and with visibility of at least 150 m. It is not compulsory to move over.

q: The right-edge line (usually on dual carriageways and freeways) …
exp: The right-edge line is usually found on one-way roads such as dual carriageways or freeways and may not be crossed.

opts.t: you may only proceed in the direction shown by the arrow in your lane

q: Mandatory direction arrows painted in your lane mean …
exp: Mandatory direction arrows (RM8): choose the correct lane in time; you may only go in the direction of the arrow.

opts.t: you may cross it when safe
it is only a guide at night

q: A channelizing line (solid line between lanes travelling in the same direction) means …
exp: Channelizing line (RM3): drive so that no part of your vehicle crosses the line.

q: An exclusive parking bay marked with the letter "L" is reserved for …
exp: RM7 letters: A ambulance, B bus, L loading zone, T taxi, F fire-fighting, CD diplomatic, MB minibus, R rickshaw, SOS phone, D defence force, P police. Only goods vehicles may stop or park in an L bay.

opts.t: Yes, in an emergency, to use the SOS telephone

q: May you stop at a parking bay marked "SOS"?
exp: In an emergency you may stop or park at the bay that indicates the SOS telephone.

opts.t: Brake hard while driving over the hump
Slow down and release your brake before driving over the hump
Speed up to cross it quickly

q: What should you do when approaching a speed hump marking?
exp: Speed hump (WM10): slow down and release your brake before driving over it.

opts.t: stop (except for pedestrians or a stopped vehicle) or overtake

q: The broken lines painted along the lane edges just before a pedestrian crossing (RM11) mark an area where you may NOT …
exp: RM11: do not stop except for pedestrians or for a vehicle that has stopped; do not overtake inside this area or a vehicle stopped at the crossing.

opts.t: the number of lanes is being reduced; change lanes in good time if yours ends

q: Lane reduction arrows painted on the road warn you that …
exp: Lane reduction arrows (WM6): change lanes in time if your lane ends, checking blind spots.

opts.t: Stop, then proceed if no traffic is coming

q: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
exp: Red means stop.

opts.t: Speed up to cross before it turns red
Stop, except where you cannot do so safely

q: What does a steady amber (yellow) traffic light mean?
exp: Amber: stop, except where it cannot be done safely.

opts.t: Go, you have absolute right of way

q: What does a green traffic light mean?
exp: Green: go if it is safe.

opts.t: Stop, and proceed when it is safe (like a stop sign)
The signal is out of order; ignore it

q: What does a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection mean?
exp: A flashing red signal means stop and carry on when safe, as at a stop sign.

opts.t: Drive on carefully, but yield to pedestrians, who may cross

q: What does a flashing amber disc mean?
exp: Flashing amber: drive carefully and yield to pedestrians, who may cross the roadway.

opts.t: You have right of way in the direction of the flashing arrow
Yield to oncoming traffic before turning right

q: What does a flashing green arrow pointing right mean?
exp: Flashing green arrow: right of way in the direction of the arrow.

opts.t: You may turn left without stopping
After stopping, you may turn left if there is no traffic, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic
No left turn at any time

q: What does a flashing red arrow pointing left mean?
exp: Flashing red arrow to the left: after stopping, you may turn if clear, yielding to pedestrians, oncoming right-turning traffic and traffic from the right.

opts.t: Stop and wait until the flashing green arrow shows you may go
Proceed with caution in the direction of the arrow
The traffic light is out of order

q: What does a steady amber arrow mean?
exp: Constant amber arrow: stop and wait until the flashing green arrow shows you may go.

opts.t: It shows the direction in which traffic must go (e.g. in one-way streets)
You may turn but must yield to all traffic
